checks.finding: Risk tiers align with each task's actual scope under the risk-classification-policy.md sentinel-surface proximity rule. T-002 (Risk: high, Security-Sensitive: true) implements Security Boundary B2, an installed-cache drift read-only comparison, matching the policy's high-tier silent-defect-material-harm definition. T-004 (Risk: high) extends the hook-guard deny-allow regression asset, an access-control-adjacent surface. T-005 (Risk: high) implements Security Boundary B1, Ed25519 signing per ADR-0028 and nonce-replay protection per security-spec.md B1 and B4, a genuine authentication and signing surface, correctly high rather than critical per its own Risk Rationale, since no financial-settlement, physical-safety, or irreversible-destructive surface is touched. T-001, T-003, T-006, and T-007 (Risk: medium) touch no authentication, authorization, payment, PII storage, data-migration, or externally-visible API-contract surface of their own; every task states Data Migration none and Breaking API no, and security-spec.md's Data Classification table records no PII or credential throughout. No proximity-rule violation found in either direction.

No Risk critical task exists in this feature. All three Risk high tasks, T-002, T-004, and T-005, carry in their own Done When sections TDD Red then Green evidence, plus in the same bullet an independent quality-gate verdict records PASS, consistent with the Lifecycle section's own statement that only quality-gate may set Done, a role structurally distinct from the implementing agent, and matching this repository's own dominant convention for this Done-When phrasing across its merged tasks.md corpus. Each of the three also carries a dedicated Requirement-traceability evidence high tier Done-When item citing risk-gate-matrix.md's high row. All required Done-When evidence items for high-tier tasks are present.

T-005, titled Author the REQ-003 live-host proof infrastructure and aggregate validator, is oversized. Its Done When list has 12 distinct verifiable items: schema and discriminator correctness, nonce ledger and signing verification, classification-mismatch and replay guard, Codex and Copilot semantic-cell classification, five-cell live-host proof handling, consumer-entry-point inventory shape, aggregate gate, draft SKIP records committed unsigned, a HUMAN APPLY STEP for Trusted-Signer Registry and two-party signing, suite and CI registration, TDD evidence, and requirement-traceability evidence, exceeding the more-than-eight oversizing indicator. Its Scope and Planned Files also span far more than three distinct implementation areas bundled into one task: schema and discriminator validation, Nonce Issuance Ledger replay protection, Expected-Digest Manifest comparison, Ed25519 signing verification under the ADR-0028 Signing Contract, the three-state SKIP Representation, aggregate-gate computation, and draft-record authoring plus Trusted-Signer Registry seeding with its own distinct human apply step. This corresponds to design.md Test Strategy items 5, 8, and 10 plus the full live-host-verification-record schema, Nonce Ledger, Expected-Digest Manifest, and Signing Contract Data Plan sections, combined into a single task. The task's own title signals two combined sequential phases, infrastructure and aggregate validator.

The tasks that author production validator or checker logic, as opposed to pure test or fixture-authoring, each have explicit edge-case or error-path coverage anchored in acceptance-tests.md. T-002's drift checker is covered by AC-022, requiring at least one independent negative-lifecycle case distinct from the always-freshly-installed happy path, and AC-023, requiring distinct not-installed, synced, and drifted states with mode-dependent FAIL semantics; both are labeled negative self-check or negative-lifecycle case in acceptance-tests.md. T-005's aggregate validator is covered by AC-026 and AC-027, exercising eighteen named error codes and an explicit classification-mismatch and replay guard labeled negative self-check, and requirements.md's Edge Cases section requires a live-host FAIL observation to be recorded as a FAIL and never silently discarded or re-run until it passes. T-007's three static checks specify mutated-copy negative fixtures for TEST-025, TEST-029, and TEST-030 in their own Scope section, each correctly rejected. No functional or validator-producing task in this feature has happy-path-only acceptance criteria.

Every row in acceptance-tests.md cites a specific AC and TEST id pair, satisfying the acceptance-test minimum for the document as a whole. Rows labeled integration genuinely span two or more system components: AC-002 and AC-003 each involve two distinct CLI runtimes producing and consuming a handoff artifact, AC-022 compares an installed cache against repository source, and AC-007 drives the install and uninstall scripts plus a drift-check sub-step. Rows labeled static or doc-review, including AC-001, AC-005, AC-011, AC-021, AC-024 through AC-026, and AC-029 through AC-030, are single-document or single-script-boundary checks, consistent with that label rather than mislabeled as multi-component integration. No test task's declared type contradicts its actual scope.

All three Risk high tasks carry an explicit Rollback field addressing safe reversion. T-002 states that reverting the task's commits is safe because nothing protected is written directly and the script never writes to the install root or the repository. T-004 states that reverting restores the file's pre-existing 101 lines exactly. T-005 states that reverting is safe because nothing protected is written directly and the five draft SKIP records remain unsigned and non-authoritative until a human completes the apply step, so a revert changes no signed security claim. Each reasons concretely, tied to the task's own protected-file or signing-state posture, about why a plain commit revert is safe.

The only files claimed by more than one task are tests/run-all.sh, tests/run-all.ps1, the staged human-copy test.yml candidate, and human-copy/MANIFEST.sha256, touched by six tasks, T-001, T-002, T-003, T-005, T-006, and T-007, each appending only its own suite's registration line or CI steps per the Deliverables table in traceability.md, and the a8-skip-allowlist.json manifest, which T-001 creates with only the AC-006 entry while T-005 later appends only the AC-015 and AC-016 entries, explicitly called out in tasks.md's own Protected Files section as the one shared, ordinary file. Both patterns are documented and additive only: each task edits distinct lines or entries for a distinct purpose, never the same content for the same purpose. No two tasks claim the same file for the same purpose without this documented coordination. The structural Blockers-field gap that leaves this documented ordering mechanically unenforced is reported once, under DEPENDENCY-OVERLAP, rather than duplicated here.

Every task's structured Blockers section reads None, including tasks whose own Depends On field, in the same document, names a genuine functional dependency. T-003's header states Depends On T-001 serialized only, and T-002 functional, because this driver invokes the drift check in verify mode as its own post-install sub-step on every cell, and the script must exist first. Yet T-003's own Blockers section is None. T-005's header states Depends On T-001 functional, because it appends the AC-015 and AC-016 entries to the a8-skip-allowlist.json file that T-001 creates with the AC-006 entry. Yet T-005's own Blockers section is likewise None. The same pattern repeats for T-002, T-006, and T-007, whose own headers cite earlier tasks as functional or serialized dependencies while every one of their Blockers sections also reads None. Task orchestration and Done-state gating in this framework key off the structured Blockers field, per the Lifecycle section's own statement that a task may enter Blocked from any active state and that implement-task may set In Progress, Blocked, or Implementation Complete. Because of this, nothing structurally prevents T-003 from being scheduled or attempted before T-002's own drift-check script exists, which T-003's Scope section says it invokes as its own post-install sub-step on every cell, or T-005 before T-001's own allowlist file exists to append to, a genuine integration-failure risk the check's own missing-blockers criterion names directly. This is the same class of gap this review's own briefing named for the sibling epic-195 task-review round, where a task's Planned Files depended on another task's output without listing that task in Depends On or Blockers. Here Depends On correctly names the dependency in prose, but the machine-actionable Blockers field is left empty across every dependent task.

SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. All seven tasks, T-001 through T-007, author net-new verification and test infrastructure such as fixtures, drivers, validator scripts, and static checks; none is scoped as a bugfix, regression fix, debugging, flaky-test resolution, or incident remediation by title, Goal, Scope, or Done When text.
